rows.label: Green tax: tourist resorts, integrated resorts, resort hotels, vessels and large hotels or guesthouses (from 1 January 2025)
rows.note: Maldives Tourism Act section 35(g) (Fourteenth Amendment, Law Number 21/2024): 'USD 12 (Twelve United States Dollar) per guest from 1 January 2025 onwards.' The green tax is paid into the Maldives Green Fund; Ministry of Finance Revenue Policy page: 'The green tax is deposited to the Maldives Green Fund; a trust fund established to earmark funds from green tax to spend on climate change mitigation measures and other environmental initiatives.' The Ministry's page attributes the 2025 rates to the thirteenth amendment of the Maldives Tourism Act; the rates are in section 35(g) and (h) as amended by the Fourteenth Amendment (Law Number 21/2024), which the page links. Unit: per tourist per day of stay.

rows.label: Green tax: hotels, tourist hotels and guesthouses on an inhabited island with 50 or fewer rooms (from 1 January 2025)
rows.note: Maldives Tourism Act section 35(h) (Fourteenth Amendment, Law Number 21/2024): hotels and tourist guesthouses 'operated in inhabited islands and have 50 (fifty) or fewer registered rooms': 'USD 6 (Six United States Dollar) per guest from 1 January 2025 onwards.' The green tax is paid into the Maldives Green Fund; Ministry of Finance Revenue Policy page: 'The green tax is deposited to the Maldives Green Fund; a trust fund established to earmark funds from green tax to spend on climate change mitigation measures and other environmental initiatives.' The Ministry's page attributes the 2025 rates to the thirteenth amendment of the Maldives Tourism Act; the rates are in section 35(g) and (h) as amended by the Fourteenth Amendment (Law Number 21/2024), which the page links. Unit: per tourist per day of stay.

sections.title: Freelancers, contractors and the self-employed

rows.label: Non-resident withholding tax on payments to a contractor (1 January to 30 August 2026)
rows.note: gross amount of a payment by a person conducting business in the Maldives to a non-resident contractor. Corrected on 2026-11-26 (was stored as 10% for the whole year): section 55(b) as amended by the First Amendment to the Income Tax Act (Law Number 15/2021, section 40) set 5% until the Second Amendment (Law Number 11/2026, in force on publication in the Government Gazette on 31 August 2026) raised it to 10%. The Ministry of Finance Revenue Policy page (dated 15 July 2025) says: 'Payments that are made to non-residents by persons conducting business in the Maldives, specified in section 55 of the Act, are subject to non-resident withholding tax at 10% or 5%.' The other section 55(a) payments were 10% throughout.

source.title: First amendment to the Income Tax Act (Law Number 15/2021): unofficial English translation

rows.label: Non-resident withholding tax on payments to a contractor (from 31 August 2026; final tax, also for a permanent establishment)
rows.note: gross amount of a payment by a person conducting business in the Maldives to a non-resident contractor (one who provides goods or services of any kind in the Maldives, or the use of goods or services of another person in the Maldives). Second Amendment to the Income Tax Act (Law Number 11/2026), section 2 (new section 55(b)); section 5: 'This Act shall commence from the date of its publication in the Government Gazette following its passing and ratification' (ratified and gazetted on 31 August 2026). The same amendment adds section 55(b-1) ('Where a payment specified in subsection (b) also falls within subsection (a), the payment shall be deemed to be a payment specified in subsection (b).') and section 27(c): the amount deducted under section 55(b) from income derived through a Maldivian permanent establishment 'shall be treated as the final tax payable by such person in respect of such income'. MIRA's NWT page lists 'Payments made to a contractor | 10% |'.

rows.label: Customs import duty: ad valorem 0% to 400%, specific duties on luxuries and goods harmful to health
rows.value: Import duty under the Maldives Export Import Act (Law Number 31/79): ad valorem rates from 0% to 400% of the value of the imported goods, specific duties on certain luxuries and goods harmful to health, or a combination of both; the President may waive all or part of the duty in special circumstances
rows.note: Ministry of Finance Revenue Policy page: 'The President has the discretion, under special circumstances, to waive import duty, or part of it, for certain imported goods.' The duty is collected by the Maldives Customs Service (customs.gov.mv), whose tariff schedule gives the rate for each heading; the per-heading rates are not stored here.

rows.note: gross amount of a payment by a person conducting business in the Maldives to a non-resident contractor. Corrected on 2026-11-26 (was stored as 10% for the whole year): section 55(b) as amended by the First Amendment to the Income Tax Act (Law Number 15/2021, section 40) set 5% until the Second Amendment (Law Number 11/2026, in force on publication in the Government Gazette on 31 August 2026) raised it to 10%. The Ministry of Finance Revenue Policy page (dated 15 July 2025) says: 'Payments that are made to non-residents by persons conducting business in the Maldives, specified in section 55 of the Act, are subject to non-resident withholding tax at 10% or 5%.' The other section 55(a) payments were 10% throughout.
rows.source_title: First amendment to the Income Tax Act (Law Number 15/2021): unofficial English translation
rows.label: Non-resident withholding tax on payments to a contractor (1 January to 30 August 2026)

rows.note: gross amount of a payment by a person conducting business in the Maldives to a non-resident contractor (one who provides goods or services of any kind in the Maldives, or the use of goods or services of another person in the Maldives). Second Amendment to the Income Tax Act (Law Number 11/2026), section 2 (new section 55(b)); section 5: 'This Act shall commence from the date of its publication in the Government Gazette following its passing and ratification' (ratified and gazetted on 31 August 2026). The same amendment adds section 55(b-1) ('Where a payment specified in subsection (b) also falls within subsection (a), the payment shall be deemed to be a payment specified in subsection (b).') and section 27(c): the amount deducted under section 55(b) from income derived through a Maldivian permanent establishment 'shall be treated as the final tax payable by such person in respect of such income'. MIRA's NWT page lists 'Payments made to a contractor | 10% |'.
rows.source_title: Second amendment to the Income Tax Act (Law Number 11/2026): unofficial English translation
rows.label: Non-resident withholding tax on payments to a contractor (from 31 August 2026; final tax, also for a permanent establishment)
